query: Counting Drops Pell distills by the drop, all night, counting aloud. "If you mean to try the old draught," he says, "you'll count with me first. Lose count once and we start again." Count all night with him Four hundred and twelve drops, and you don't lose count once. At dawn Pell says "Fair," which is once a decade, and lets you stopper the bottle. You lose count at three hundred and something. Pell starts again without comment. So do you. You lose it again. Go home and sleep You go home. Pell counts on alone, steadily, through the night. In the morning the bottle is full and labelled, and he says nothing about it.
